text: How the watcher's lease works, for D-0069. It's the ref `refs/invariant/lease`, pointing at an empty commit whose message names the holder and when its lease runs out. Taking or renewing it is a `git push --force-with-lease` that names the commit the watcher read, so git refuses it, under the ref's lock on the server, if another watcher moved the ref first. A watcher's name is random, so the ref says nothing about the machine. The holder checks it every poll, in the background, so it keeps the lease through agent runs, and pushes a renewal once half the lease has gone. It stops acting a minute before its lease runs out by its own clock, and another watcher takes it only a minute after, by its own, so clocks a minute apart can't let two act. The holder checks the lease before every post, label, push, pull request, merge, branch deletion and agent run. A lease lasts five minutes by default, and at least three polls.
